label: prop:cusp-shape-bar-parity
title: Cusp-shape bar-parity: the figure-eight modulus splits as $\mathfrak{V} = \mathrm{Vol} + i\,\mathrm{CS}$
html:
Proposition. Cusp-shape bar-parity: the figure-eight modulus splits as \mathfrak{V} = \mathrm{Vol} + i\,\mathrm{CS}

The cusp shape of the figure-eight knot 4_1 is \omega = e^{i\pi/3}, a primitive sixth root of unity — the root of the cyclotomic polynomial \Phi_6(z) = z^2 - z + 1 in the upper half-plane, with trace field \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-3}). Split \omega along the bar-involution \sigma\colon x \mapsto x^{-1} into its symmetric and antisymmetric shapes:

  \mathrm{barEven}(x) = x + x^{-1}, \qquad \mathrm{barOdd}(x) = x - x^{-1}.

Then the cusp shape realizes the two faces of the Neumann–Zagier complex volume \mathfrak{V} = \mathrm{Vol} + i\,\mathrm{CS}:

  \mathrm{barEven}(\omega) = 1, \qquad \mathrm{barOdd}(\omega)^2 = -3.

The bar-even part is the rational Volume normalization 2\cos(\pi/3) = 1; the bar-odd part is the \sqrt{-3} Chern–Simons modulus (2i\sin(\pi/3))^2 = -3.

The identity holds over any field carrying a root of \Phi_6. From \omega^2 - \omega + 1 = 0 one gets \omega^{-1} = 1 - \omega (since \omega(1-\omega) = 1), whence

  \mathrm{barEven}(\omega) = \omega + (1 - \omega) = 1,
  \qquad
  \mathrm{barOdd}(\omega) = 2\omega - 1,

and (2\omega - 1)^2 = 4\omega^2 - 4\omega + 1 = -3 using \omega^2 = \omega - 1. It is formalized sorry-free as cusp_barParity_split over a generic [Field R] (no archimedean structure).
